clue.text: Beast allowed round to get to work

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, a beast
let means allowed
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A creature permitted a lap before starting its labours.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle to is an idiom for setting about a job with energy.

clue.text: Transporter not training people to work

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle that is not a train, read as 'not train-ing'
to man a post is to supply people to work it

explanation.surface: A vehicle that skips the railway carries staff to their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not training' is read as 'not a train', the road vehicle; 'people to work' is the verb sense, to staff something.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus driver carries passengers about, so is a transporter of people.

clue.text: Striker offering could be exposed

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman, the striker, who offers a catch is dismissed this way
found out in a lie or error

explanation.surface: A batsman's edge could leave him dismissed and shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the striker is the batsman facing the bowler; offering a catch gets him dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman offering a catch gets dismissed, and a person shown up in deceit is also found out.

clue.text: Left gulf port with a full cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port on the Gulf of Aden in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship sails from a Gulf harbour fully loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded, as a ship with a full hold.

clue.text: Stuff Welsh river before tea break

parts.note: the Taff flows through Cardiff in Wales

indicators.note: the word tea is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Eat your fill by a Welsh river before the tea interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a tea break but signals an anagram of TEA, giving ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven fabric, and this is a crisp silk fabric.

clue.text: One politician by statute orders strike

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP is a Member of Parliament
an act is a statute passed by a parliament

explanation.surface: An MP brings in a law ordering a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit or collide with something is to make a forceful contact, a synonym.

clue.text: Month spent on parade

parts.note: March is a month
past means over and done, spent

explanation.surface: A month used up on military parades.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial procession of troops saluting a dignitary is a type of parade.

clue.text: Member newsman equipped

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
ED is short for editor, a newsman

explanation.surface: A journalist on the staff came well kitted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed means furnished with weapons, so equipped for a fight.

clue.text: Score half to string together drink

parts.note: a score is twenty, and half of it is ten
to twine is to twist strands together

explanation.surface: Halve the tally to link up the beverages.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red Spanish wine once used for communion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is a sweet red Spanish wine, so this is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Talk loudly in silence apparently

definitions.meaning: to speak out forcefully and opinionatedly
with the audio switched off, as a television in silence would be

explanation.surface: Ranting while seemingly saying nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: the sound is off, so all is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout opinions is to holler forth, and literally the audio being switched off means quiet.

clue.text: Railways point to soldiers in Germany

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in Germany, a noun phrase for the city

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail
E is east, a point of the compass
men are soldiers, the other ranks

explanation.surface: Trains bring troops to a destination in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Bremen is a port city in northern Germany, an example of a place there.

clue.text: First category

definitions.meaning: chief or leading, as in the leading chef
a division or section under which items are listed

explanation.definitionFit: The chief of something is foremost, and items filed 'under this' sit in one class or heading.

clue.text: He's an eccentric, pale

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are set in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd fellow with a wan complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' describes the man on the surface but asks for an anagram of HESAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey-white like ash, drained of colour.

clue.text: Make-up by sight-screen

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight
to shadow is to shade or screen

explanation.surface: Cosmetics next to a cricket sight-screen.
explanation.walkthrough: A sight-screen is the white board behind the bowler in cricket; here it splits into 'sight' and 'screen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured powder for the eyelids is a cosmetic, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Argument against prisoner drawing back

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: back tells us the word for drawing is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: drawing is art

explanation.surface: A case put by an inmate who withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing back' looks like retreating; it is ART reversed, TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Contra is Latin for against, used for a counter-argument, as in pros and contras.

clue.text: Bound to find accommodation in pub

parts.note: tied means bound
a house is a place to live, accommodation

explanation.surface: Certain to get a room at the inn.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIED HOUSE is a British pub owned by a brewery and obliged to sell its beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery-owned bar that must stock its owner's beer is a kind of tavern.

clue.text: Doctor gets a clown to soldier

parts.note: a goon is a fool or buffoon, a clown

explanation.surface: A physician recruits a joker for the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Oil supplier with many 9 branches

parts.note: reads like a petrol company with lots of outlets, but means a fruit-bearing plant that yields oil and has many boughs; the 9 is a stray print mark

explanation.surface: A fuel company with a large chain of filling stations.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'branches' are boughs, not shop outlets, and the oil comes from pressed fruit. The '9' in the clue as held is a stray print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Its fruit is pressed for cooking oil, and as a plant it has numerous boughs.

clue.text: Hide from neat young thing's family

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so its young is a calf, with the possessive S
kin means family

explanation.surface: Concealing oneself from a tidy youngster's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy but is the old word for cattle, whose young is a CALF.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather made from young cattle is a hide, an animal's skin.

clue.text: Simple philistine

definitions.meaning: a person lacking in culture, with no art

explanation.definitionFit: Being guileless is plain and naive, and lacking culture literally means without art.

clue.text: Overruling objections to what's left of ticket

indicators.note: in a down clue, ruling over means the word for objections is turned upwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: A judge dismisses complaints about a torn ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overruling' looks legal but reverses BUTS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The counterfoil left after a ticket is torn is its remnant.

clue.text: Particular dock

definitions.meaning: to dock an animal is to cut off its tail

explanation.definitionFit: An individual point is a specific item, and de-tail literally means remove the tail, as docking does.

clue.text: Reactionary stamp firm

parts.note: a die is a tool for stamping metal
hard means firm

explanation.surface: A conservative company that makes rubber stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard resists all change, a conservative reactionary.

clue.text: Blackguard going with daughter is fly

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel, a blackguard

explanation.surface: A rogue courting someone's daughter is sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis fly is an insect whose larva builds a case in streams.

clue.text: Box-office hit by card player's good hand

definitions.meaning: a performance with every seat sold
in poker, three of a kind with a pair

explanation.definitionFit: A sold-out theatre has all seats taken, and in poker three of a kind plus a pair is a strong hand.

clue.text: Slip into sound circuits

indicators.note: sound says the word for circuits is heard, not seen

parts.note: laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: Fall into healthy laps of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy but tells you to say LAPS aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief error or failing is a slip.

clue.text: Cockney institution Georgia considers the end

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so a care home becomes 'ome
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: A London care home in Georgia thinks about death.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner who drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the final thing, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Another form etc to complete composition

indicators.note: the letters of etc to are given another form, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Rewrite the et cetera to finish the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of music for eight players is a type of composition.

clue.text: Continued to be supported

explanation.definitionFit: Maintaining an effort is carrying on, and being held aloft is being propped.

clue.text: Yorkshire is given a hammering

parts.note: reads as a county team beaten heavily, but a Yorkshire pudding is made of batter, so it is coated in batter

explanation.surface: The Yorkshire team suffers a heavy defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yorkshire pudding is a British baked side dish made of batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten heavily and also made of batter, as a Yorkshire pudding is.

clue.text: Scene I make with some of the family

indicators.note: make tells us to make something new out of the letters of scene I

explanation.surface: A family drama's opening scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters of one's siblings are relatives, members of the family.

clue.text: Die out on lock with woman ahead on paper

indicators.note: out means the letters of die are put out of order

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A woman leading a newspaper dies with a lock of hair on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A female in charge of a newspaper is an old term for a female editor.
